62895142.s: At-Turaif District has been one of the most important political and geographical sites in Saudi Arabia since the founding of the First Saudi State. It lies in the heart of the Arabian Peninsula, in Diriyah northwest of Riyadh, and was the first capital of the Al Saud family.
62895142.b: At-Turaif District has been one of the most important political and geographical sites in Saudi Arabia since the founding of the First Saudi State. It lies in the heart of the Arabian Peninsula, in Diriyah northwest of Riyadh, and was the first capital of the Al Saud family. Founded in the 15th century, At-Turaif preserves the Najdi architectural style unique to central Arabia. In the 18th and early 19th centuries its political and religious role grew, and it became the seat of Al Saud power and a centre for the spread of the Salafi reform movement in Islam. The district contains the remains of many palaces, as well as a town built on the banks of the Diriyah oasis. At-Turaif District in historic Diriyah was inscribed on UNESCO's World Heritage List in 1431 AH (2010).

62625727.s: Ain Balta is an ancient spring, once flowing and surrounded by palm trees, set among the Aja mountains along the Shu'ayb Al Hamra and Al Jadam valleys, which drain into Wadi Al Salaf. It still exists today and is mentioned in the poetry of Imru' al-Qais, Salam ibn Amr ibn Dirma al-Ta'i and others.
62625727.b:
Ain Balta is an ancient spring, once flowing and surrounded by palm trees, set among the Aja mountains along the Shu'ayb Al Hamra and Al Jadam valleys, which drain into Wadi Al Salaf. It still exists today and is mentioned in the poetry of Imru' al-Qais, Salam ibn Amr ibn Dirma al-Ta'i and others.

From Yaqut al-Hamawi's Mu'jam al-Buldan:

Balta is said to be a well-known place in the two mountains of Tayyi'. It was the home of Amr ibn Dirma, with whom Imru' al-Qais ibn Hujr al-Kindi stayed as a guest seeking protection, and he said:

I stayed with Amr ibn Dirma at Balta

How fine a neighbour, and how generous a host

Imru' al-Qais also said:

Whenever I feared injustice one day

I had a ravine at Balta, a refuge

60169885.t: Najran Heritage Village and Dahda Museum
60169885.s: Najran Heritage Village and Shu'ayb Dahda Museum is a heritage destination in Najran that introduces visitors to Najran's mud-brick architecture and to everyday items from the region's past.
60169885.b:
Najran Heritage Village and Shu'ayb Dahda Museum is a heritage destination in Najran that introduces visitors to Najran's mud-brick architecture and to everyday items from the region's past.

The museum takes its name from nearby Shu'ayb Dahda, an important archaeological site where stone tools attributed to the Oldowan culture were found. They are estimated to be more than a million years old and include choppers, scrapers, blades and hammerstones, making the area one of the oldest sites of human settlement in the Arabian Peninsula.

60169883.s: Abu Saq Kahilan Historic Palace is a heritage building in Najran that reflects the traditional Najrani architecture of mud built up in successive layers. It is a destination for heritage and photography enthusiasts.

60169880.s: The Hima Cultural Area, also known as Bir Hima or the Historic Hima Wells, is a World Heritage site in the Najran region of southern Saudi Arabia. It contains more than 34 sites rich in rock inscriptions and wells along one of the oldest caravan routes crossing from southern Arabia to the north. The Hima Cultural Area rock art covers 557 square kilometres and includes 550 rock-art panels with hundreds of thousands of inscriptions and drawings depicting hunting, animals, plants and ways of life of a culture that continued without interruption for 7,000 years. It is one of the largest rock-art complexes in the world.

60169785.s: Wadi Najran is one of the largest valleys in Saudi Arabia and the largest in the Najran region. It divides the city of Najran into northern and southern parts. Its tributaries come from the Hijaz mountains (the Sarawat) and the surrounding Asir plateau, and it runs 180 kilometres east from its mouth on the plains, ending in the sands of the Empty Quarter. Its average width on the plains is 1,000 metres.

60169703.s: Uruq Bani Maarid Reserve is a nature reserve in southern Saudi Arabia, under the supervision of the National Center for Wildlife, on the western edge of the Empty Quarter, the largest sand desert in the world, in the Najran region. It is considered the last place where the Arabian oryx was seen before it became extinct in the wild in 1970. The reserve contains a number of important landforms and natural habitats, including high sand dunes and a broken limestone plateau, and is divided into three zones: the core zone, a zone where controlled grazing is permitted, and a hunting zone.
60169703.b:
Uruq Bani Maarid Reserve is a nature reserve in southern Saudi Arabia, under the supervision of the National Center for Wildlife, on the western edge of the Empty Quarter, the largest sand desert in the world, in the Najran region. It is considered the last place where the Arabian oryx was seen before it became extinct in the wild in 1970. The reserve contains a number of important landforms and natural habitats, including high sand dunes and a broken limestone plateau, and is divided into three zones: the core zone, a zone where controlled grazing is permitted, and a hunting zone.

Uruq Bani Maarid lies in an area that was home to the Arabian oryx before it disappeared from the wild. The remaining area was chosen for the reintroduction of oryx raised in captive breeding programmes, and was also chosen as suitable for restoring herds of Arabian sand gazelle, mountain gazelle and ostrich, all of which historically lived in the area.

In 2023, Uruq Bani Maarid Reserve was inscribed on UNESCO's World Heritage List, the first natural site in the Kingdom to be listed.
